lessons.title: First Watt
lessons.concept: Power: kW is a rate, capacity is a ceiling, and load above capacity means a blackout.
lessons.goal: Two racks, one day, no blackouts.

steps.text: Build your first rack on the glowing slot
say: Bea Altasar, power. Welcome to the hall. One job today: two racks, running a full day, and nothing goes dark.
Open Racks in the build bar, pick the AC-1 and drop it on the glowing slot. Everything else stays locked till it's in.
after: Hear that? 40 kW, flat out. A {{kw|kW}} is a rate: how hard something is pulling right now. The bar up top is the whole hall, 93 kW, against the feeder's 120. Remember that 120.

steps.text: Build a second rack on the next slot
say: {{capacity|Capacity}} is the most a supply can give, and this feeder tops out at 120 kW. The hall burns 53 before a single rack works (air handler, lift, the intake itself), and one rack takes it to 93. Put the second one in. Watch the bar.
after: And there it goes. Two racks want 133 kW, the feeder gives 120, and the breaker does what breakers do. Load over capacity is a blackout. Every time. The whole job is keeping capacity above load, with {{headroom|headroom}} to spare.
Power overlay's on, so you can see the net. Now the part I hate: a generator.

steps.text: Add the diesel generator in Power
say: Power tab, the Diesel Genset, the glowing slot. It starts itself when the grid can't keep up.
A {{genset|generator}} adds capacity: 120 from the feeder plus 800 from the diesel. It also adds smoke, and it doesn't wash out. Today it's the right tool. Later we'll talk about better ones.
after: That gap between what you can supply and what you're using is {{headroom|headroom}}. Lots of it now. Hold both racks flat out for one game day and you've passed.

steps.text: Hold both racks at full load for one day
say: Let the clock run. Keep headroom above 10% all day and don't let anything go dark. I'll be watching the meter. And the exhaust.

lessons.learned: {{kw|kW}} is how hard equipment pulls right now; {{capacity|capacity}} is the most the supply can give. Keep capacity above load, with {{headroom|headroom}} to spare.
lessons.outro: Two racks, a whole day, lights on. Good. Next time I'll show you power that doesn't come out of a tank. Come find me when you want to learn where all this heat ends up.
